cities.base: Downtown/Centro, near Plaza de la Independencia, for walkability to the sights and the Costanera
cities.name: Asuncion

places.name: Jesus de Tavarangue ruins
places.note: A reduction church that was never finished, so the arches and red sandstone stand raw and unroofed; the carved stone doorway is the piece to see. Covered by the 40,000 Gs ($6.47) combined ticket; 07:00 to 18:30 in winter, later in summer, check. Videomapping Friday and Saturday nights.

places.name: Palacio de López
places.note: The seat of government, seen from the street with no public hours (Google 4.6, 1,099 reviews); it is lit at night, so pass again after dark. Fodor's mentions Thursday and Friday tours by advance arrangement, undated, so check before counting on one.

places.name: Casa de la Independencia
places.note: Small colonial house where the independence conspirators met in 1811; give it 45 minutes. Weekday hours differ by source (from 07:00 or 08:00 to 16:30 or 18:30) and Saturday ends at 12:00 or 13:00, so hours vary, check, and check the price: none is published.

places.name: Mercado Cuatro
places.note: Sprawling working market, not built for visitors, with cheap lunch stalls; watch your bag. Weekdays it runs 07:00 to 18:00, but Saturday it shuts at 11:30 and Sunday it is 08:00 to 11:30, so a morning is the safe plan.

places.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta
places.note: Above-ground mausoleums of the old elite, where Elisa Lynch, presidents Aceval and Morínigo and Serafina Dávalos are buried; Asociación Mandua'ra runs night tours. No entry price is published, so check the price, and listed hours vary, check.

places.name: Costanera de Asunción
places.note: Riverfront promenade along the Paraguay River, good for an evening walk with families and joggers out. Not much shade midday, better after 5pm.

places.name: Manzana de la Rivera
places.note: Free cluster of restored colonial houses on the city's history, opposite the Palacio, with Casa Clari inside. Fodor's has 07:00 to 21:00 weekdays and 10:00 to 21:00 weekends, older listings say shut Sundays, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Panteón Nacional de los Héroes
places.note: Small domed mausoleum for the national heroes with guards outside, free every day; 15 minutes. Weekdays it runs to 17:00 or 18:30 depending on source, Sunday to 12:00, and it can shut for ceremonies, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Catedral Metropolitana de Asunción
places.note: Plain cathedral with an unremarkable interior, free, and twenty minutes is plenty. Fodor's (undated) gives 09:00 to 11:30 and 18:00 to 20:00 daily, but it has been found shut at Sunday midday, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Lido Bar
places.note: Counter diner since 1953, on Independencia Nacional since 2022; order the vori vori. Asuncion Times (Dec 2024) paid 37,000 Gs for vori vori, bread and a cola, $5.98 at the BCP rate. The bill is slow, so ask early.

places.name: Mercado Central (Mercado Modelo)
places.note: Smaller and more manageable than Mercado Cuatro, good for ao po'i embroidery and ñandutí lace souvenirs without the chaos.

places.name: Santísima Trinidad de Paraná (Jesuit Ruins of Trinidad)
places.note: UNESCO-listed and the best preserved of Paraguay's Jesuit reductions; do not miss the carved stone on the facade and pulpit. The 40,000 Gs foreigner ticket ($6.47) covers all three missions for 72 hours. Day hours run to 17:00 or later by source, check; the night light show starts 19:00 to 19:30.

places.name: Museo de Sitio Trinidad
places.note: Small on-site museum (a 2026 blog counts two, one in the church sacristy) with recovered stone pieces and context panels, no charge beyond the 40,000 Gs combined ruins ticket. Ten to 30 minutes on the way in or out; site hours, check.

places.name: Sacristia y Museo de Sitio
places.note: Small museum room with fragments, maps and an explanation of the reduction system, no charge beyond the 40,000 Gs combined ticket; no separate hours found, check. Skip it if you did the Trinidad museum, it covers the same ground with less.

places.name: Parroquia Sagrada Familia
places.note: The town's working parish church, modern and modest, useful only as contrast to show what replaced the Jesuit-era building. Not worth a special trip on its own.

places.name: Ruinas Jesuiticas de San Cosme y Damian
places.note: The least restored of the three, with astronomy interpretation tied to the Jesuit Buenaventura Suárez. The guided visit is included in the 40,000 Gs ($6.47) combined ticket and usually needed to get inside; posted hours run to 18:30 or later, check.

places.name: Planetario Municipal
places.note: Small, low-budget planetarium tied to the observatory theme, only worth it if it's actually open and staffed that day, which is not guaranteed.

places.name: Bolsi
places.note: Centro comfort food on TasteAtlas's iconic-restaurant list, Google 4.6 from 16,820 reviews. Asuncion Times (Dec 2024, updated Aug 2025) paid 67,000 Gs for dieta de aves, an empanada and a 500ml beer, $10.84 at the BCP rate; empanadas are the cheap order, cards taken.

places.name: Karu
places.note: Bakery and cafe with a weekly set menu at 38,000 to 45,000 Gs ($6.15 to $7.28 at the BCP rate, Asuncion Times Feb 2025), served 11:00 to 15:00 and 17:00 to 22:30; brunch is about 50,000 Gs. Weekdays it opens 07:30, and a Wednesday market runs 08:30 to 14:00.

places.name: Casa Clari Cafe & Bar
places.note: Cafe-bar inside Manzana de la Rivera, opposite the Palacio de López, open to 01:00 Friday to Sunday. A Caesar salad and pink lemonade came to about 90,000 Gs (Asuncion Times, Feb 2025), $14.56 at the BCP rate; Google 3.9, so come for the spot, bring cash, groups book.
places.neighborhood: Centro histórico, Manzana de la Rivera

places.name: Centro Cultural de la República El Cabildo
places.note: Free cultural centre in the old Cabildo, Google 4.5 from 1,182 reviews; give it an hour. Wanderlog has 07:00 to 17:00 weekdays and 09:00 to 17:00 weekends, Fodor's has 09:00 to 19:00 and shut on Mondays, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Museo del Barro
places.note: The city's best-rated art museum on Google (4.7, 1,204 reviews); allow 90 minutes. Wanderlog lists $8.36 and some free days, undated, so check the price, and its hours differ from Fodor's: hours vary, check, but Wednesday to Saturday late afternoon suits both.

outings.why: The two Jesuit mission ruins, done together as a full day including the drive between them.
outings.name: Trinidad and Jesus de Tavarangue

outings.why: The smaller Jesuit ruin with the old observatory, further out and lower key than Trinidad.
outings.name: San Cosme y Damian day trip
outings.fallback: Skip it and do the Encarnacion riverfront and market instead if you're tired.

destination.name: Paraguay
destination.pitch: A week for the Jesuit ruins around Encarnación and a capital city with no tourist infrastructure at all, which some people find refreshing and others find exhausting by day four.
destination.caveat: There is very little built for tourists here, so days can feel like logistics rather than sightseeing. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Asuncion is a working capital with almost no tourist gloss on it, which is its own kind of interesting.
because.food: Mercado Cuatro is a real market, not a curated one.
because.culture: The Jesuit ruins at Trinidad and Jesus de Tavarangue are the real reason to come.
because.exploration: San Cosme y Damian and the ruins circuit reward people who like figuring things out on the ground.
